summary: Production verification accepts runtime assertion JSON whose producer and raw browser observations are not bound to the evidence. Introduce a fail-closed browser evidence bundle so screenshots, interaction, accessibility, overflow, and component-runtime assertions are traceable to one current browser session and hashed raw artifacts.
decisions: Runtime JSON is evidence only when it is bound to a versioned browser session, current runtime-tree digest, and hashed raw observations; free-form passed=true assertions are not sufficient.

Codex Desktop QA must use the in-app Browser skill for the actual run and then register its screenshots, DOM/state observations, console logs, and accessibility/overflow results through the harness contract.
The Python harness validates and ingests browser outputs but must not pretend it can invoke a privileged browser backend that is only available to the agent runtime.

gate_results.evidence: The current interaction report contains narrative assertions but no browser producer identity, session binding, or hashed raw artifacts.
Existing tests pass without proving that a browser produced the runtime assertions.

risks: Producer metadata is not a cryptographic attestation by itself; independent Production QA must still inspect raw artifacts and tool execution history.
A browser bundle requirement must not silently accept old runtime-check/v1 files as production evidence.
next_action: Production QA implements and documents a versioned browser evidence bundle/validator, integrates it as a blocking production gate without weakening component runtime conformance, updates the QA skill to execute the in-app browser workflow, and returns a ready handoff with tests and current hashes.
